> LLM-generated review from https://github.com/canonical/maas-code-reviewer.
> Intended to assist a human reviewer, not replace one — suggestions may be
> incorrect, please verify before acting.


Docs-only change; prose is accurate, well-linked (I verified every internal target and anchor resolves: `myst_heading_anchors = 4` in docs/conf.py:460 covers the h3 anchors `#delete-a-rack-controller` and `#manage-api-keys`, and `/reference/cli-reference/config-vault.md` is generated at build time by docs/_scripts/generate_cli_docs.py:49,813). Structure matches the existing how-to conventions (`## Before you begin` / `## Related topics`), and both the list and the toctree in docs/how-to-guides/index.md were updated.

Two substantive problems, both from the new Mermaid dependency:

1. Offline/hardened rendering. MAAS ships these docs inside the snap (snap/snapcraft.yaml:324 `offline-docs`, `MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true make html`, served from `usr/share/maas/web/static/docs`), and hardened region controllers serve them under `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-...'` (src/maasserver/templates/http/regiond.nginx.conf.template:65). sphinxcontrib-mermaid's default `mermaid_output_format = 'raw'` emits an inline module script that imports `mermaid.esm.min.mjs` from jsdelivr (upstream README, `mermaid_use_local` section), so the new diagram will silently fail to render in air-gapped and hardened deployments — exactly the reason the Ubuntu fonts were vendored (docs/_static/fonts/README.md:29-47).

2. Non-HTML builders. .readthedocs.yaml declares `formats: [pdf, htmlzip]` and docs/Makefile:161 has a `pdf` target; for any non-HTML builder sphinxcontrib-mermaid shells out to `mmdc` (mermaid-cli, Node), which neither RTD's build config nor `REQPDFPACKS` (docs/Makefile:16) installs. Upstream documents the required RTD `post_install: npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` plus `mermaid_params = ["-p", "puppeteer-config.json"]`.

Content-wise, the decommission guide has a gap that matters for its own stated goal ("without leaving data, credentials, or references behind"): snapd snapshots and non-rack components. Details inline. CI coverage for this change is `make lint-md` + `make html` (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:206-223); `make html` uses `--fail-on-warning`, so please confirm the Mermaid page builds clean there, and ideally check `make pdf` locally given point 2.

docs/conf.py.354: Enabling the extension with defaults means the HTML output loads `mermaid.esm.min.mjs` from jsdelivr at runtime (default `mermaid_output_format = 'raw'`, `mermaid_version = '12.0.0'`). Two concrete consequences for MAAS: (a) the docs shipped in the snap (snap/snapcraft.yaml:324) are served offline, so the diagram stays blank; (b) hardened/FIPS regions set `script-src 'self' 'sha256-...'` (src/maasserver/templates/http/regiond.nginx.conf.template:65), which blocks both the CDN fetch and the injected inline module script. Vendor `mermaid.esm.min.mjs` under `docs/_static/vendor/` and set `mermaid_use_local = "vendor/mermaid.esm.min.mjs"`, following the precedent (and README) established for the Ubuntu fonts in docs/_static/fonts/. If the inline init script still trips CSP, prefer `mermaid_output_format = "svg"` so the diagram is baked into the page at build time.

docs/requirements.txt.23: For any builder other than HTML, sphinxcontrib-mermaid renders via `mmdc` (mermaid-cli, Node + puppeteer). .readthedocs.yaml requests `formats: [pdf, htmlzip]` and docs/Makefile:161 defines `make pdf`, and neither installs Node/mermaid-cli (`REQPDFPACKS` at docs/Makefile:16 only lists TeX/plantuml packages). As-is, the PDF build of this page will fail or drop the diagram. Either add the upstream-documented RTD `post_install: npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli` (+ `puppeteer-config.json` and `mermaid_params = ["-p", "puppeteer-config.json"]`), or pre-render the diagram to SVG and avoid the runtime dependency entirely.

docs/explanation/security.md.15: Diagram source is fine, but it is the only copy of this information in a non-text form — worth confirming it renders in the snap-served docs build (`MAAS_OFFLINE_DOCS=true make html`) before merge, not just on readthedocs. See the conf.py comment.

docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.35: The revocation list misses the two credential classes the new "Inherent risks" section in explanation/security.md calls out as highest value: BMC credentials and the rack/region shared secret. Both existed in the database and in every backup you just told the reader to keep, so they must be rotated on the hardware, not just deleted from MAAS. Suggest adding: "Change the BMC credentials of every machine MAAS managed" and "Treat the MAAS shared secret as compromised if backups are retained."
docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.39: Only rack controllers are covered. Two gaps: (1) region controllers (including the common region+rack install from how-to-guides/get-started/install-maas.md) are never deleted from MAAS, and in HA deployments there are several; (2) POC installs use the `maas-test-db` snap (see how-to-guides/back-up-maas.md:10, which dumps from `/var/snap/maas-test-db/common/postgres/sockets`) — that snap also holds MAAS credentials and needs `sudo snap remove maas-test-db --purge`.
docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.44: `--purge` only suppresses the *automatic* snapshot taken at removal; snapshots created earlier by `snap save maas` — which how-to-guides/back-up-maas.md:54 explicitly instructs readers to create — survive and remain readable under `/var/lib/snapd/snapshots`. They contain the full MAAS data directory, i.e. secrets. Per the snapcraft decommissioning guidance, add a step: `snap saved` to list, then `sudo snap forget <set-id>` for each MAAS snapshot.
docs/how-to-guides/decommission-maas.md.51: This verification does not detect the leftover state described above. Add `snap saved` (must list no MAAS snapshots) and `ls /var/lib/snapd/snapshots`. Also note the expected output of these commands: after a successful purge, `snap list maas` prints `error: no matching snaps installed` and exits non-zero, and `ls /var/snap/maas/` errors with `No such file or directory` — otherwise readers will read the failures as a problem.
